body.statement: There is an interval specified by \(def:robust-heavy-light-interval-handle\) such that, for every \(d\le c_{\epsilon}n\log(en)\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}Q_P^{(n)}\{\tau(P)\in\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[|\widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}|]\lesssim_{\epsilon,\alpha}r_{n,d,M}\). The guarantee uses only the observed sample, the known values \(M\), \(\epsilon\), and \(\alpha\), and the conditions defining \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}\).
body.justification: The theorem remains the desired constructive half of the honest-length frontier, but it is not proved by the available deterministic light-bias result.
body.gap: Neither the light score radius nor the winsorized heavy self-normalized Gaussian/fallback radius is currently an explicit valid sample map, so coverage and expected length remain open.
body.consumer: The intended consumer is a uniformly valid replacement for the reference intervals in the Zeng et al. 401(k) analysis.

obligation.what_is_open: Finite-sample coverage and expected-radius bounds for an explicit heavy-light interval on the unrestricted global class.
obligation.obstruction: The rare score is unresolved for the reasons recorded on \(oeq:observable\text{-}rare\text{-}tail\). The heavy branch is also not a sample map: no winsorization threshold, deterministic fourth-moment truncation allowance, aggregate self-normalized score, Gaussian/fallback switching rule, or score radius is defined. Consequently neither allocated score event can be proved, and the all-heavy identity required for local equivalence is absent. The deterministic light-bias lemma cannot imply honesty.
obligation.attempted: I decomposed the ATE error into pilot, light bias, light fluctuation, heavy truncation bias, and heavy fluctuation terms and allocated the requested \(\alpha/4,\alpha/4,\alpha/2\) error levels. Only the deterministic light-bias term closes from the current core. The proposed symmetric score fails the root audit before a direct MGF proof, and there is no heavy summand on which to perform the corresponding fourth-moment calculation.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved node \(lem:four\text{-}coordinate\text{-}bias\) supplies the
deterministic light-branch bias allowance
\(C_\epsilon Md/[n\log(en)]\).  If measurable light and heavy radii
\(R_{\mathrm L},R_{\mathrm H}\) obeyed, on one common pilot-good event,
\[
 Q_P\{|T_{\mathrm L}-E(T_{\mathrm L}\mid I_0)|>R_{\mathrm L}\mid I_0\}
 \le\alpha/4,
 \qquad
 Q_P\{|T_{\mathrm H}-E(T_{\mathrm H}\mid I_0)|>R_{\mathrm H}\mid I_0\}
 \le\alpha/2,
\]
and had expected radii of orders
\(M\{n^{-1/2}+d/[n\log(en)]\}\) and \(Mn^{-1/2}\), respectively, while
pilot failure and the pilot-dependent conditional means were controlled at
level \(\alpha/4\), then the triangle inequality and a union bound would give
coverage \(1-\alpha\); clipping to \([-2M,2M]\) would not enlarge length, so
integration of the two score tails would give the claimed expected-length
order.  The current core proves only the displayed deterministic bias term.
